subject: Business
title: How Banks Make Money
description: A micro-lesson that makes How Banks Make Money usable.

hook.text: A bank pays you 0.5% on your savings. It lends that same money to someone else at 7%. The difference is profit.

buildup.text: The net interest margin — the spread between deposit rates and loan rates — is a bank's core revenue.

discovery.text: Banks also earn from fees: overdraft charges, ATM fees, credit card processing, and wealth management.

twist.text: Banks lend out far more money than they hold in deposits. This 'fractional reserve' system multiplies money supply.

climax.text: JPMorgan Chase earned $49.6 billion in 2023. Most came from lending your deposits at higher rates.

punchline.text: Your savings account isn't storing money. It's lending it to the bank cheaply.

quiz.question: What is a bank's 'net interest margin'?
options: The difference between what it pays depositors and what it charges borrowers
The bank's total revenue from fees
The interest a bank earns on government bonds

details.summary: Banks profit primarily through the interest rate spread, charging borrowers higher rates than they pay depositors. Additional revenue comes from fees, investment banking services, and trading activities. Understanding this model reveals why banks incentivize certain products.
details.whyItMatters: Knowing how banks earn money helps consumers make better financial decisions. When you understand that banks profit most from high-interest lending and fees, you can avoid costly products and negotiate better terms.
takeaways: The interest rate spread between lending and deposit rates drives core bank profits
Fees for overdrafts, maintenance, and services add substantial revenue
Banks lend out far more than they hold in deposits through fractional reserves

faq.question: How much of your deposit does a bank actually keep on hand?
faq.answer: Banks typically hold only a fraction of deposits in reserve, often around 10 percent or less. The rest is lent out to earn interest. This fractional reserve system means banks create money through lending but also introduces systemic risk if many depositors withdraw at once.

faq.question: Why do banks offer free checking accounts if they need to profit?
faq.answer: Free checking attracts depositors whose money the bank can lend at higher rates. The bank profits from the spread. Free accounts also create cross-selling opportunities for credit cards, mortgages, and investment products that generate fees and interest income.
